text:
incidents-bot: Paging @maggie (oncall) — SLO breach detected for dedicated pool 'eu-west-2a-prod'  — p95 > SLO and p99 spike, streaming stalls reported. AlertID: INC-2169876543

maggie (oncall): acked. I'm seeing the alert dashboard. p95 ~ 2.3s -> 3.1s last 5m, p99 ~ 12.7s -> 28s. Streaming stalls spikes at ~00:15 UTC.

samir (eng-sre): joining, looking at pool metrics. Queue depth for that pool jumped from 120 -> 970 in 6m. Warmup queue is 610.

reza (eng-runtime): obs: autoscaler requested +30 nodes at 00:12 but cloud returned capacity slowly. Handshake/warmup latency for new instances ~45s each, so effective capacity came late.

kai (eng-platform): checking autoscaler logs now. Looks like warmup timeout 60s, but we have an extra prewarm handshake step that adds ~20s per node. Also some startup script contention.

ellie (support): customers reporting "generation stalls" in chat. One customer (acct: acme-retail) saw token gap >30s and aborted. Ticket #6543 opened.

jordan (product): any evidence of cascading fallback to hosted variants? Could avoid blocking customer apps if fallback was used.

reza (eng-runtime): fallback routes are in place but policy requires warmup success before routing. We didn't failover because fallback threshold is conservative.

samir (eng-sre): immediate mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily reduce required warmup handshake (if safe) 2) increase fallback aggressiveness 3) manually add a few pre-warmed instances (hotshot) 4) throttle low-priority customers to relieve queue.

maggie (oncall): let's run mitigations in parallel. Reza, can you enable fallback to the compatible smaller-quantized variant for the tail of the queue? Kai, can you manually spin up hotshot pre-warmed nodes? Samir, coordinate throttles and customer comms with Ellie.

reza (eng-runtime): initiating fallback toggle: `POST /api/v1/route/policies/fallback -d '{"pool":"eu-west-2a-prod","fallback":"v2-small-quant"}'`

ops-bot: Request accepted. Change queued for deployment to routing layer.

kai (eng-platform): kicking manual pre-warm: `./tools/hotshot create --pool eu-west-2a-prod --count 8 --prewarm true` output: 
```
submitted: 8 nodes
expected warmup per node: 40-50s
current pool target: 40 -> 48
```

maggie (oncall): samir, throttle plan?

samir (eng-sre): starting a soft throttle on non-SLA tiers: `redis-cli -h qmgr incrby queue:throttle:eu-west-2a 1` and bump rate limiter for free-tier to 10r/min. Applying now.

ellie (support): emailing affected accounts with status. Notifying Acme that we're actively mitigating and will follow up.

reza (eng-runtime): fallback routing change deploying now. Expect to see queued requests drain to compatible variant within ~15s of deploy.

maggie (oncall): timeline note: alert at 00:10, autoscale requested at 00:12, warmup slow, manual interventions starting 00:18. Current p99 improved?

samir (eng-sre): p95 at 00:25 down to 1.9s, p99 down to 9.4s but still above SLO. Queue depth from 970 -> 320 after throttle + fallback. Warmup hotshots still coming online.

reza (eng-runtime): logs show a subset of requests are streaming (long-living sessions) that tie up KV cache warmups and block preemption. Considering early token-level prefetch to warm KV for streamed sessions.

kai (eng-platform): hotshots reporting 6/8 ready at 00:31. New capacity mostly cut queue. Autoscaler logs show cloud API rate-limited for some nights — need escalations to cloud account team.

maggie (oncall): customer impact tracker: Acme (high), BetaCorp (medium), smaller apps (low). Ellie please update support channel and set ETA 1h for post-incident report.

jordan (product): we should update fallback policy to trigger earlier on queue depth and on streaming stall signals, not just static latency threshold. Add to follow-ups.

ellie (support): Acme confirmed partial recovery, will retry flows. Ticket updated.

samir (eng-sre): post-mitigation checks: p95 1.4s, p99 3.8s at 00:45. Streaming stalls count down to single digits. Queue depth stable ~40. Taking incident to monitoring phase.

reza (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: burst of traffic + insufficient pre-warmed capacity + misaligned autoscaler warmup/handshake settings -> delayed effective capacity -> queue amplification -> tail latency. Secondary contributor: conservative fallback policy and some long-lived streaming requests that blocked efficient batching.

kai (eng-platform): immediate action list I just applied: 1) increase prewarm pool target by 10% for burst windows 2) lower handshake wait time to bypass non-essential checks during high queue depth 3) escalate cloud quota rate-limit to provider support.

maggie (oncall): owners and follow-up items: 
- samir: postmortem + timeline (ETA 24h)
- reza: automated earlier fallback policy by queue-depth/stream stall signals (ETA 48h)
- kai: infra change to reduce warmup handshake + test hotshot fast path (ETA 72h)
- ellie: customer impact summary + CS outreach notes (ETA 6h)

samir (eng-sre): creating incident channel #incident-2169876543 for postmortem notes. Will include logs, grafana links, and runbook actions.

maggie (oncall): handing back to normal ops. If any p99 > SLO re-alerting triggers, repage. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Incident state changed to MONITORING. Incident INC-2169876543 assigned to samir (eng-sre).
